statusText: Tail eases to 21%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. The 31,119.75 session low has now held for more than two hours, NQ Dec26 has recovered to 31,218.25 and the loss has narrowed to -0.59% from -0.78%, while VIX slipped to 15.57 from a 16.02 session high. The long end has backed off its peak, with the 10-year at 5.29% and the 30-year at 5.66% against 5.33% and 5.70% an hour earlier, so Stress eases to 65% but stays in the high band. Hormuz tanker strikes still hold Brent near 104 and WTI near 92 at roughly +4%, and semiconductors lead the pre-market lower.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 21%, inside the 20-24% band and below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30Z-15:00Z, spanning the U.S. cash open and the first full cash hour, where conditional Tail peaks at 25% and maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Conditional Tail eases to 24% at 15:00Z, forms a secondary 24% ridge across the 17:00Z 30-year auction and the 17:40Z Fed Musalem speech, and returns to the EA_ON band from 20:00Z as the cash session completes. Stress at 65% remains the dominant reading: the environment is difficult and may still mean-revert. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend a two-hour hold above the session low as the long end backs off its peak, easing Tail while the Hormuz oil shock keeps Stress high
body:
The fourteenth Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session continued the repair that began an hour earlier. NQ Dec26 trades 31,218.25 as of 13:14Z, -184.00 or -0.59% against a 31,402.25 prior close, corroborated independently at 31,225.00 with a matching -0.56% and the same 31,402.25 reference. The 31,119.75 low that printed in the 11:00Z hour has now stood for more than two hours, price sits roughly 99 points above it, and the day's loss has narrowed in two steps from -0.78% to -0.70% to -0.59%. VIX has eased further to 15.57, +3.25%, from a 16.02 session high. The overnight range of 31,119.75 to 31,410.75 is an orderly 0.93%.

The more consequential change this hour is in rates. The long end has backed off the peak that drove the previous two hours of risk: the 10-year prints 5.29% against 5.33% an hour ago, and the 30-year 5.66% against 5.70%, with the 2-year little changed at 4.81%. That partial reversal removes one of the three amplifiers that had been operating together, and it is why Tail steps down to 21% rather than holding the 22-23% of the previous two hours. A session low that goes unextended for two hours while the loss narrows, implied volatility decays and the driving yield move partially retraces is a failed downside extension. It is the opposite of the repeated extension after failed retracements that defines a pathological price path.

Two amplifiers do remain intact. A record week of Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes, with UK officials reporting at least nine attacks in the waterway so far in October and the conflict entering its eighth month, still holds WTI at 91.68 and Brent at 104.26, both near +4%. And semiconductors lead the pre-market lower: SOXX trades 572.73, -1.73% against a 582.82 close, roughly three times the index decline. Downside semiconductor leadership is a genuine Tail amplifier if it persists into the cash session, which is the single reason the conditional path peaks at 25% in the 14:00Z hour rather than easing straight through the session.

Today's one scheduled U.S. release has already printed. Initial jobless claims came in at 197,000 for the week ended October 3 against a 200,000 consensus, with the prior week revised to 199,000 and the four-week average down to 198,000; continuing claims rose to 1.716 million. Claims have held near 57-year lows for four consecutive weeks, which sits awkwardly against September payrolls of just 29,000 and reinforces the hawkish rates narrative behind a 5.66% 30-year. The reaction was muted, consistent with the Aug 7 precedent in which a far larger labour-market surprise did not become a lethal no-retracement path.

The U.S. cash open at 13:30Z is not yet observed at this assessment time, so no opening-auction structure is claimed. That checkpoint, and the 17:00Z 30-year auction into a long end near a 24-year peak, are the two credible conditional mechanisms in the window. Stress eases one point to 65% and stays in the high band: the oil shock, the yield level and the semiconductor leadership make this a difficult environment that has nonetheless kept mean-reverting all session.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 13:00Z trace one complete risk cycle and the start of a second. Tail ran 22-23% through Wednesday's European and early U.S. hours, eased steadily to a 10% trough by 03:00Z as the overnight session mean-reverted, then rebuilt from 06:00Z as the Hormuz oil shock and the long-end yield move reasserted themselves, reaching 23% at 11:00Z when a three-hour base at 31,196.75 gave way to the 31,119.75 low. Stress rose almost monotonically across the window, from 53% to 66%, which is the clearer signal: the environment deteriorated steadily while the price path kept retracing. Every hour stayed in the EA_ON or WATCH band, and no hour reached the 25% blocking threshold. Confidence held in a tight 86-89% range throughout.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail is concentrated in the U.S. cash session rather than spread across the window. It rises from 21% now to a single 25% peak in the 14:00Z first full cash hour, the only slot mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, and the narrow 13:30Z-15:00Z danger window covers the cash open and that hour. A secondary 24% ridge at 17:00Z spans the 30-year auction and the Fed Musalem speech, reflecting a credible delayed second-leg mechanism into a long end near a 24-year peak rather than observed structure. From 20:00Z the cash close returns Tail to the EA_ON band, and it bottoms at 13% through Asian hours before drifting back to 19% by the 12:00Z window close, one hour ahead of Michigan sentiment. Stress follows a shallower arc from 65% to a 50% overnight trough and back to 58%, staying above Tail throughout, because the oil and rates backdrop is a difficult environment rather than evidence of a pathological path. Confidence decays from 88% to 75% purely with forecast horizon.
